_comment: Public-SDK-only namespace policy for extension packages (M9-A3, #951).
This file is the machine-readable half of the public/private boundary.
scripts/check-extension-imports.py reads it and enforces it against every
extension tree listed in extension_trees. The boundary it encodes is the
one ADR-081226-034b states in prose: extensions build on public extension
contracts, never on product-private internals.
policy_version          Version of this policy document's own shape.
public_sdk_namespaces   First-party import roots an extension MAY import.
Today exactly one: the versioned extension SDK
package (M9-A1, #949). Everything else first-party
is product-private by default.
product_private_namespaces  First-party import roots an extension must
never import. Underscore-prefixed modules are
private even under a public root, and repo-relative
roots (packages.*, extensions.*) are forbidden
outright - those rules live in the gate, not here.
extension_trees         Glob patterns (repo-relative) of directories that
are extension packages subject to this policy.
Each matched directory must hold a pyproject.toml,
i.e. it must be buildable on its own.
test_only_namespaces    Import roots a test file may use without declaring
them as runtime dependencies (test tooling is not
a shipped dependency). Outside a tests/ directory
these are undeclared-dependency violations.
required_artifacts      File names every extension wheel must ship, as
verified from the installed distribution by
scripts/check-reference-extension.py. Today the
discovery manifest: a wheel without it installs
but can never be discovered by a host.
Classification is closed: every import root shipped under packages/*/src
must appear in exactly one of the two namespace lists, so a new product
package cannot quietly become importable from extensions by being
forgotten here. The gate checks that direction too.
